### Run it live

My worst bugs passed every mocked test. I run the real provider, unintercepted, before I call anything done.

If a rule matters, code checks it after generation. Prompts ask nicely. Validators refuse.

About

# Hi, I'm Suyash.

I'm an AI engineer and full stack developer. I build LLM systems with guardrails and evals, and I do forward deployed work: sit with the people using the system, ship what they need, and leave something the next person can maintain.

Bio

## What I do

I build LLM systems end to end: guardrails, evaluation pipelines, and the application code around them. I test against live providers and write evals that say what they cannot claim.

At Anterra Corp I fine-tuned YOLOv8m and integrated BoT-SORT tracking on Jetson Orin Nano edge hardware. I built a custom Nepali Devanagari ANPR model and demonstrated the traffic violation detection system to senior police and ministry officials.

On freelance projects I work directly with the people using the software. I have sat with factory workers to refine inventory workflows and with school administrators and teachers to fix bugs in an academic management system.

## Work Alignment

Source: https://www.suyashbhattarai.com.np/work-alignment

# Representation alignment

A toy-scale test of unsupervised alignment between two independently trained encoders, with controls and held-out retrieval checks.

Role

Research design, implementation, and analysis.

Stack

Python, PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn

Protocol

Held-out retrieval, unrelated-encoder control, and diagnostics.

Scope

Synthetic scenes and independently trained toy encoders.

## Start with the reference

The implementation centers and normalizes each space, constructs relative representations, obtains an initial correspondence with clustered similarity structure and QAP restarts, then fits an orthogonal Procrustes map. Two refinement stages alternate nearest-neighbor matches and map updates.

## Independent encoders

## Checks before interpreting it

### Split and control checks

The train and evaluation scene indices were separated, and an unrelated-encoder control was carried through each alignment run. The write verification recorded a clean result.

### Procrustes was not enough for identity retrieval

### Known rotation behaved differently

### The proxy was not the outcome

## Evidence for correspondence at toy scale.

best independent-encoder shape accuracy with relative representations

mean cosine for that aligned pair

shape accuracy for the corresponding unrelated control

## Work Entode

Source: https://www.suyashbhattarai.com.np/work-entode

Case study 02, 2026

# Entode

I built a backend generator around a reviewed schema, a deterministic compiler and a bounded agent loop. The compiler builds the app structure, models fill the business logic, and executable checks drive the repairs.

Role

Solo builder. Architecture, compiler, agent harness, evaluator and UI.

Stack

Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, pytest, React, React Flow

Output

Auth, relational data, row-level permissions, encrypted fields, and REST APIs

Code

Private. Happy to walk through the architecture.

01

## The idea

A short request can describe an app, but it cannot settle every decision about data, access, and behavior. I wanted the generated backend to have an architecture I could inspect before treating the code as finished.

Entode holds that architecture in one internal representation. The ERD, business-logic and state-machine view, generative design surface, and running app all come from it. A change to the design reaches every view without a separate copy to keep in sync.

02

## The pipeline

- Propose. A schema model turns the request into architecture changes. I review the proposal before accepting it into the JSON schema.

- Compile. A deterministic compiler emits FastAPI routes, SQLAlchemy models, request and response schemas, and the declared permissions.

- Write. A separate code model fills marked business-logic stubs. Larger jobs are split into function chunks, and only the permitted functions are merged back.

- Evaluate. Static checks inspect the code and protect compiler-owned parts. Generated pytest cases exercise the app through HTTP requests, including behavior across routes.

- Repair. The evaluator recursively feeds failures back into generation. Each correction starts from the clean compiler baseline and the latest failure report.

The schema proposal and code-generation stages have separate responsibilities. A failed code attempt cannot silently redefine the architecture it was asked to implement.

03

## Where the model can write

The compiler owns the permission dependencies, state-transition helpers and encryption runtime. The code model implements the business logic around them. Integrity checks compare these protected parts against saved compiler output, so a rewritten permission check cannot pass just because the rest of the route still works.

### Fresh context for each correction

I restore the compiler stub before every correction. The next attempt receives the schema, the clean stub and a concrete report of what failed. Failed code and a growing chat history do not become the next attempt's starting point.

The loop stops when the checks pass, failures repeat, or the attempt budget runs out. It also stops when the failure belongs to the schema or compiler; rewriting business logic cannot fix those problems. The remaining failure is surfaced for a decision.

04

## The test that changed the result

The running app had to prove the wiring.

End-to-end evaluation

### Every earlier check passed. One route was still wired wrong.

A generated backend passed the other checks in the pipeline, but an end-to-end test found a real cross-route wiring defect. The individual pieces looked correct; the request path through the running app was not.

That case is why the evaluator exercises behavior across routes, rather than accepting code shape or isolated route checks as proof. The model that wrote the code does not decide whether the result passes.

05

## What it produced

From the sentence "build a basic social network," Entode generated a backend with auth, a relational data model, RBAC with row-level permissions, encrypted fields, and a REST API. The useful part was being able to inspect the schema and check the generated behavior against it.

I also exercised the pipeline against six application archetypes: marketplace, CRM, booking, helpdesk, LMS, and ticketing.

Passing the configured checks tells me how the app behaved on those cases. Entode is a local development tool; a generated app still needs deployment review and tests for requirements its schema does not describe.

## Work Evalgate

Source: https://www.suyashbhattarai.com.np/work-evalgate

# Evalgate

A Rust evaluation runner and CI gate for live or recorded model outputs. Define weighted checks in YAML, classify repeated runs, and report score regressions.

Role

Solo project. Design, implementation, and site integration.

Stack

Rust, Tokio, reqwest, serde_yaml, wasm-bindgen, GitHub Actions

Links

Live demo, GitHub

Code

Open source, on GitHub.

## The problem

Prompt changes ship without tests. A wording tweak in the system message, a new few-shot example, or a model swap can pass code review and break production behavior. Regressions show up as customer complaints, not CI failures.

Evaluation should support live endpoints during development without making CI depend on API keys. Evalgate uses the same YAML schema for OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, echo, and recorded replay targets. The replay path keeps pull request runs deterministic.

## How it is built

The workspace separates pure evaluation logic, asynchronous IO, and browser bindings:

- evalgate-core. Validates suites, renders templates, evaluates checks, scores weighted results, classifies repeats, and builds reports without doing IO.

- evalgate-cli. Executes live or replay targets with bounded concurrency, rate limiting, retries, request timeouts, disk caching, and snapshot storage.

- evalgate-wasm. Exposes deterministic evaluation, report comparison, and a flaky classification example to the browser demo.

### Decisions that mattered

- Repeat classification. --repeat records a case pass rate and distinguishes stable passes, stable failures, and partial flaky results.

- Checks at different layers. Text, regex, JSON shape, similarity, latency, cost, snapshot, LLM judge, and embedding checks feed one weighted score.

## What was hard

Parts that took more than one pass.

### Keeping network behavior testable

### Flaky cases need their own status

A case that passes some samples is different from a stable regression. The report keeps pass rate and flaky state alongside weighted check results, so comparison output does not collapse intermittent behavior into one verdict.

### Snapshots are explicit

Snapshot checks accept a first output only with --update-snapshots, then compare later output against that saved value.

## Measured, then stated.

optimized WASM binary with the size-focused release profile

named check kinds in the suite schema

## Work Flamide

Source: https://www.suyashbhattarai.com.np/work-flamide

Case study 01, 2026

# Flamide

I co-founded Flamide and built the product, now in beta with select education consultancies. Its AI agent handles Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp enquiries in Nepali, English and Romanized Nepali. It collects student details, updates the CRM and follows up on conversations. Counselors take over when a case needs their judgment.

Role

Co-founder and sole engineer. Product, agent workflow, backend and UI.

Stack

Next.js 16, TypeScript, Supabase (Postgres, RLS, Realtime), DeepSeek, Vitest, Playwright

Status

Beta deployment with select consultancies.

Code

Private. Happy to walk through it on a call.

01

## The problem

Consultancies in Nepal run on DMs. Most enquiries come in after hours, in mixed script, and ask the same handful of questions about courses, fees and intakes. The answers need to come from the consultancy's current catalog.

The expensive messages are the other ones. "Will my visa get approved?" "I was refused last year." "Can you lower the fee?" A confident but unsupported answer can change a student's plans. The counselor needs to see these cases with enough context to take over.

I built the workflow around the consultancy's own data and explicit handoff rules. The counselor gets the conversation and the reason it was escalated.

02

## How it's built

The agent does more than draft replies. Student details from a conversation are extracted into a validated set of CRM fields. Follow-ups use the conversation history and pass through reply checks before they enter the delivery queue. Sensitive cases carry a reason and summary into the counselor handoff.

The main reply path works like this:

- Inbound checks. Prior refusals, complaints, finance questions and requests for a human can trigger escalation before reply generation.

- Generate. A six-layer prompt: style, guardrails, domain reference, consultancy identity, catalog, then conversation state.

- Outbound checks. Code checks for visa predictions, unsupported numerical requirements and claims attributed to the wrong university.

- Repair. A guardrail failure gets one regeneration with the violation named. Script and provider-format failures have their own bounded recovery paths.

- Escalate. If it still fails, the conversation goes to a human with the reason attached.

### Decisions that mattered

-  Workspace isolation is enforced in the database. Workspace-scoped records use row-level security policies and composite (workspace_id, id) foreign keys. The database rejects references across workspaces instead of leaving that check to each screen.

-  CRM updates have a narrow write path. Extracted fields are validated with Zod and passed to scoped SQL functions with the workspace and source message attached. Internal university fields stay out of prompts through an explicit column allowlist, checked against the schema.

-  The prompt keeps a stable prefix. Workspace instructions, domain reference and catalog context precede the changing conversation state. This gives the provider a reusable prefix without assuming that every request will hit its cache.

-  Replies wait in a durable queue. Workers claim jobs with a lease and record completion transactionally. Pending replies can be recovered after a restart; external delivery still needs to account for a send succeeding before its completion is recorded.

-  Transport sits behind a channel adapter. Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp sit behind ChannelAdapter. The core workflow stays separate from each platform's payloads and can be exercised through a mock adapter during development.

### Staff can query the pipeline too

A separate assistant turns staff questions into validated filters and groupings. Application code applies them to the caller's records and calculates the counts. The model helps interpret the question; it does not invent the result or run arbitrary SQL.

03

## What broke, and what I changed

The parts a demo never shows.

Incident

### Green suite, silent product

The first live call to the model returned nothing. Every reply, every time. In the "careful" effort mode the model spent the whole token budget reasoning and got cut off before writing a character, and the engine quietly logged that as "silent." The mock-provider tests had missed the failure because their responses had no token ceiling.

I sized the ceilings per effort level from measured completions, added a guard that fails loudly on an empty completion, and started treating live runs as a separate gate.

Incident

### Every fact true, the sentence false

A reply told a student that CQUniversity needs 75% for CBSE students. CQUniversity had no CBSE requirement on file, and 75% belonged to Coventry, in another country. Each piece was real, so an existence check could never catch it.

The guardrail now validates the whole tuple (university, board, value) against the database, and a missing row counts as a violation. That turns "requirement unknown" into an escalation instead of a guess.

Incident

### The provider answered with 86 spaces

Certain JSON-mode requests came back as pure whitespace with a normal stop reason, deterministically, at temperature 0. I isolated the trigger to the JSON-mode flag with five variations of the captured payload.

The engine now retries that one turn without the flag and parses the result through the same reader. It's documented as a mitigation rather than a fix, because the provider behavior is still unexplained.

04

## How I check behavior

Mock-provider tests cover the application's decisions. Database tests check isolation and constrained writes. Browser tests exercise the counselor workflow. These answer different questions, so a green unit suite does not stand in for all of them.

I also use scripted live-model evaluations to inspect replies and guardrail behavior in English, Nepali and Romanized Nepali. They produce conversation reports for review; they are not an automatic guarantee that a model change is safe to ship.

05

## Limits, stated plainly

- The product is in beta with select consultancies; the case study describes that stage of deployment.

- The reply checks cover specific failure patterns. They do not catch every unsupported claim, especially requirements stated only in prose.

- The live evaluation runner records outputs for inspection. A passing automated canary for the current model is a separate piece of work.

## Work Fx

Source: https://www.suyashbhattarai.com.np/work-fx

# Corridor FX

Role

Solo. Engine, dashboard, and models.

Stack

Python, FastAPI, XGBoost, Vite, React, TypeScript, recharts

Corridor

USD/NPR proxy from public INR per USD daily observations

Demo

Run the forecast and hedge demo

Code

Private. Walkthrough on request.

## The problem

Separately, margin leaks in three places: unhedged Convert Later risk net of hedge cost, idle Nostro balances sitting below the NRB deposit rate, and customer markup that could move by a basis point. The operator needs those buckets sized in one place, not spread across spreadsheets.

USD/NPR on a managed peg is not a directional bet. Risk is basis points per cycle. The product value is VaR, hedging, and idle-capital opportunity cost, not pretending to call the next move.

## How it's built

FastAPI serves a Python engine split into four modules: data.py, exposure.py, margin.py, and forecast.py. A Vite + React + TypeScript dashboard reads the API and charts the series with recharts.

- Margin out. Three buckets: unhedged Convert Later risk net of hedge cost, idle Nostro opportunity cost at the NRB deposit rate, and customer-markup yield with per-basis-point sensitivity.

- API surface. /api/overview, /api/series, /api/positions, /api/exposure, and /api/margin expose the same logic the UI uses.

Risk statistics are empirical from NRB USD/NPR daily rates. The sample position book is synthetic, seeded to simulate a Dashain-season surge so hedge logic is demonstrable without a live feed.

## What I chose not to oversell

Honesty as a design constraint.

### Held-out quantile loss beats a random-walk baseline

### Monthly remittance from press reports, not blocked PDFs

## Measured on NRB data.

## Work Openswitch

Source: https://www.suyashbhattarai.com.np/work-openswitch

# Open Switch

A Rust LLM gateway with deterministic routing simulation, provider fallbacks, per-key budgets, and streamed OpenAI-compatible responses.

Role

Design and engineering

Stack

Rust, axum, WebAssembly, vanilla JS

Repository

GitHub ->

## The routing decision is a moving target.

A deployment can look cheap and healthy until a run of failures or a latency spike changes the tradeoff. The routing core is deterministic and separate from HTTP, so the browser demo can exercise the same decision model without contacting a provider.

The axum gateway accepts OpenAI-compatible chat requests, lists configured models, emits SSE for streaming responses, and exposes plain-text request and latency metrics.

## Failure has a state machine.

A deployment breaker starts closed, opens after consecutive failures, and later admits a limited half-open probe set. Successful probes return it to closed. The simulation exposes that state for every deployment after a run.

Latency is an exponentially weighted moving average. Unlike a fixed window, the alpha makes the reaction speed explicit. Cost-aware routing selects the cheapest healthy choice within a configured latency budget.

## Protect the slow tail with a second attempt.

When the first request crosses the hedge delay, the gateway starts the next deployment and uses the first completed answer. Tokio cancels the losing attempt when the request future is dropped. The simulation reports hedge count and modeled tail latency saved.

Bearer keys have token ceilings per minute. Model groups and prices stay in deployment configuration, and mock, OpenAI-compatible, and Anthropic adapters share the request shape at the gateway boundary.

## Small enough to inspect.

tests passing in the workspace

optimized browser WebAssembly binary

## Work Quint

Source: https://www.suyashbhattarai.com.np/work-quint

# Quint

A deterministic choice-and-reveal system for AI user interfaces. Most LLM products still behave like terminals: text in, text out. Quint gives developers explicit control over what a button sends to the model, what the user sees locally, and where that content appears. Provider-agnostic, and it runs without any LLM at all.

Role

Solo. Library, docs, and demo apps.

Stack

Shipped

Demo

Try the live demo

Code

GitHub, npm

## The problem

In a standard chat UI, a multiple-choice question has two bad options. Show the answers immediately and you spoil the question. Hide feedback at the bottom of the thread and you break spatial context.

Roleplay branches have the same issue. A choice should open a local description under the button that caused it, not dump another paragraph into an endless scroll. The model input and the user-visible reveal are often different things, but most chat components treat every click as raw text.

Quint is the layer between your conversation history and your UI. You already own model calls, retries, and rate limits. Quint owns how a decision becomes a structured choice and a localized reveal.

## API design

The surface is small on purpose. A Block holds content and an array of Choice objects. Each choice declares directionality and reveal routing explicitly.

- out. Reveals pre-supplied hiddenContent only. No LLM request.

- in. Sends structured inputData to your handler. Response lands in the main chat stream.

- in-n-out. Both: local reveal plus model input, for tutoring hints or branching scenes.

- Reveal routing. reveal: true anchors content in a collapsible container under the button. reveal: false keeps it in the global stream.

### Minimal usage

Core state lives in src/core. React bindings export QuintProvider, QuintRenderer, BlockRenderer, ChoiceButton, and RevealContainer, plus hooks like useAddBlock and useUpdateRevealContent for LLM-filled reveals.

## What Quint is not

Scope by exclusion.

### Not a chat framework, not an AI SDK

Quint does not manage conversation history, call models, run RAG, or route tools. It is not an agent runtime. Those stay in your app. Quint only structures how a user action becomes input and how feedback appears in the layout.

That narrow scope is why it ships with zero runtime dependencies beyond React itself, and why MCQs can use directionality: 'out' with hiddenContent for deterministic feedback with no extra token spend.

### Three provider integrations, not part of the package

The demo/ folder has self-contained apps for Gemini, OpenAI, and Claude. Each shows how to wire onChoiceActivated to a provider and push generated text into a reveal with useUpdateRevealContent. They need API keys and are reference only, not published to npm.

# Savings score stress test

A simulation of what happens when bars optimize toward a savings score of the kind insurance-tech vendors advertise.

Role

Simulation, analysis, and independent audit.

Stack

Python, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, matplotlib

Design

Data boundary

Only NYC feature distributions are real. Premiums and losses are generated.

## What is simulated

A hidden management-quality variable affects both loss and observable proxies such as cameras and paperwork. A carrier fits a Tweedie GLM to observable features; a monotone gradient-boosting score estimates premium reductions from operational changes. Venues take their top three recommended actions, then the carrier refits over ten periods.

## What the baseline showed

## What survived the audit

### The full-adoption recovery was not a rebalancing effect

### Correction needed an almost direct management signal

### Proxy attribution held, calibration did not

## Work Screener

Source: https://www.suyashbhattarai.com.np/work-screener

# Screener

Role

Sole author. Design, implementation, eval, and demo.

Stack

Rust, wasm-bindgen, postcard, arXiv metadata (CC0)

Scope

Links

Live demo, GitHub

## The problem

Keyword search misses paraphrases. "Policy gradient training" will not match a paper that only says "reinforcement learning" in the abstract. Vector search fixes that, but it misses exact terms and typos. A query for "informtion retrieval" should still find information retrieval papers.

## Design

The pipeline splits cleanly into build time and query time.

screener-core has no IO. The CLI builds indexes and runs evals. screener-wasm exposes one constructor and a query method that returns JSON.

## What was hard

Details the README skips.

### WordPiece on full abstracts

### Tokenizer parity with the reference

### FST build on load

Building the term FST eagerly during engine construction trapped WASM with an unreachable panic on the full corpus. Lazy initialization on first query fixed it without changing search behavior.

## Measured on the eval set.

gzip transfer payload for the search assets

rebuilt postcard index

arXiv papers (cs.CL, cs.LG, cs.IR metadata)

## Try it

Try the live demo or browse the source on GitHub.
